mechanism_narrative: The observed gradual recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks (from -25.4% to -22.0%) indicates a persistent underlying trend of increasing public engagement with retail and recreation venues, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in PARKS mobility, especially when it crosses a threshold of -15% from baseline (currently -11.9%), indicates increased public comfort with outdoor activities, which often precedes or coincides with increased comfort for other public spaces like retail, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -15% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in WORKPLACES mobility (from -24.3% to -30.1%) and an increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 18.9% to 19.9%) suggests a return to work-from-home patterns, reducing discretionary trips to retail and recreation venues during weekdays, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls and RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls and RESIDENTIAL rises, but RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of stable or slightly declining transit usage, a sustained low level of TRANSIT mobility below -35% (currently -33.7%) indicates a lack of confidence in public transport, which restricts access to city centers and retail hubs, thus depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -35% but RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility drops below -2% from baseline (currently -2.3%), it signals a general reduction in essential outings, indicating heightened caution or reduced need for movement, which will also negatively impact discretionary RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -2% but RETAIL_REC increases in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in PARKS mobility (from -18.9% to -11.9%), coupled with a stagnant or slightly declining RETAIL_REC, suggests a substitution effect where people prefer outdoor recreation over indoor retail, diverting activity away from retail venues and leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by >5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC changes by <1 point
failure_condition: PARKS rises significantly while RETAIL_REC is flat, but RETAIL_REC subsequently increases over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 22.4% to 19.9%) indicates people are spending less time at home, which frees up time for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease, but RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks is lower than the previous four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where businesses are encouraged to reopen, a significant drop in WORKPLACES mobility (from -24.3% to -30.1% week-on-week) signals a reversal of reopening efforts or increased caution, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC as fewer people commute and engage in associated retail activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC increases in the subsequent week.
